newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Arafat begins New York visit with gala reception.
newsitem.headline: Arafat begins New York visit with gala reception.

text.p: Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat briefs the U.N. Security Council on Wednesday shortly before it debates Israel's decision to build a new Jewish neighbourhood in East Jerusalem.
The council debate had been postponed a day at the request of the United States, whose ambassador, Bill Richardson, said he wanted Arafat's discussions in Washington to end first.
Arafat arrived at the United Nations late on Tuesday for a gala reception of well over 1,000 people sponsored by Palestinian Americans from the New York area.
The reception included an array of U.N. officials and diplomats, including those from Israel, as well as many people from outside the United Nations.

U.N. security guards, fearing that the reception room that holds 1,200 would become overcrowded and block fire exits, kept many waiting a floor below for more than an hour as the receiving line inched past Arafat.

Arafat was also scheduled to confer with Secretary-General Kofi Annan before leaving for Houston, Texas, late on Wednesday for meetings with former President George Bush and former Secretary of State James Baker.

In Washington on Tuesday, he told a press conference he had no alternative to pursuing peace talks with Israel and still saw Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu as a partner despite his decision to build the new housing.
But he again bitterly denounced the Israeli decision to build 6,500 new homes in mainly Arab East Jerusalem, calling it an illegal move that created a "real challenge" to the peace process.
The Palestinian leader said the move violated commitments by Israel's former Labour government not to alter the demographic balance in the area until the peace process was complete.
